_source: Each entry is a claim our profile (gdl/designsys/afterburn.json) or its README made that Afterburn's own pages contradict, found by the grammar measurement of 2026-10-22: every page and popup of seeds/Afterburn 1035.gdl, 725, 525, 320, 1230W, 1535 and the 300M pair, read with gdl.project (each control's rect, look, caption and font) beside its renders and beside the 1220, 1020, 1520, 520, 535 and 320 Series templates. `template` is what those pages do, off the seed and pages named; the region frame (panels[series].frame) is the same seeds measured by tests/measure_series.py frame_of. `python -m gdl.designsys audit afterburn` checks every resolution against the profile, the README and the frame as they stand.

entries.claim: The Rail README says its children stack 'down it in order', a Slider taking 'the length the others leave'.

template.does: Afterburn's right rail is not one stack: the Volume heading is at 160 (level with the left rail's first heading), the slider runs 202-597, Mute overlaps the slider's foot at 594, an empty band follows, and Help and Power sit side by side in one row (1125,706 and 1197,706). An optional top slot is at 30. The column is centred on x 1193, not the rail's centre 1189.5.

entries.reason: The Rail stacks its children on every panel (docs/claude-design.md section 4), which is how the 520, 320 and 300 columns fit a small screen; it cannot put Help and Power in one row or let Mute overlap the slider. On the panel the canvas is drawn on a Rail stands at the right rail's band, as the template's column does, and stacks there too: one rule for the column on every panel, where placing it by hand on the drawn panel left a designer two contradictory ones and the template's own 8 px pair under the 2 mm gate. The README says so, and what the template does.
entries.here: A Rail stacks its controls down the right rail on every panel, the drawn one too: the template's column does not - its Volume heading level with the left rail's first heading, Mute over the slider's foot, and Help and Power side by side.

entries.claim: The Rail and Slider READMEs say that on a panel without a slider the slider 'becomes a Level with Down and Up buttons at its ends', and the README says 'a level between - and +'.
where: README Every panel the room has

template.does: The 520 and 535 stand Up and Down together at the top of a column with Mute at the bottom, beside a full-height level (525 Start: level 670,113, 15x314; Up 705,113; Down 705,194; Mute 705,361). On Main the level is a separate 50x480 'Volume Level' popup at 637,0, left of a rail of Up, Down, Mute, Help, Settings and Power. The glyphs are up and down triangles, not - and +; only the 300M uses minus and plus, in a row with Mute under a horizontal level.

entries.reason: The Rail builds the volume of a panel whose seed has no slider as a level between two buttons of the panel's own look (bundle.js asLevel), with `-` and `+` as their words. Extron's triangles are glyphs of its Afterburn icon font, which a design system does not carry (the owner allows the kit's PNGs, not fonts); the kit draws the same triangles as images in Afterburn/Icons/PNG (Carets' caret-up-gray and caret-down-gray), and the 300M's minus and plus (minus, plus), but this system's kit root is Afterburn/Buttons/PNG, so its `icon` list does not name them and a level's `steps` cannot yet (docs/ROADMAP.md). The README says what the template does.
entries.here: On a panel with no slider the volume is a level between `-` and `+` buttons; the template's are up and down triangles, glyphs of a font the system does not carry.

No volume, Help or Power is on screen; the volume is the modal 'Volume Level' (level 288,25, 15x190 on a #BABCCE strip at 270,0). The 300 Portrait's footer holds Settings, Help and Power on Main, with Back and the title elsewhere, and puts the volume in the main region; the 300 Landscape's right column holds Settings, Help and Power, not the volume. The 520 and 535 rails add a Settings gear.

entries.reason: Afterburn draws its chrome as background art, not controls (`layout.bars` is not `controls`), so its system has no region components: its small panels re-lay a Page's controls in rows over a Rail across the foot. The 320's page per source under a title strip, More and Back, and its Volume modal are built for the bar themes only (the region frame spec, item 7). The README says what the template does.

entries.claim: The icon variant and Iconography say 'a stand-alone control (help, power, close, mute) is variant="icon"' and 'Every icon comes from Afterburn's own resource kit'.

template.does: The template's Close, Back, More, d-pad, transport, zoom, scroll and screen arrows are glyphs in the 'Extron-Afterburn' icon font (25-90 pt, #BABCCE or #767789) on plain or outlined buttons. The kit draws most of them as images too, in Afterburn/Icons/PNG beside the Buttons/PNG the system reads: Close's X (440x440_close.png), Back's and the 320's More's chevrons (Chevron's chevron-left and chevron-right), the scroll and volume triangles (Carets, in #BABCCE and #767789), the More dots (more) and most of the transport keys. None is in the system's `icon` list, which is read from Buttons/PNG, so the Close the README called an icon button was not one it offers.

entries.reason: The glyphs are characters of Extron's Afterburn icon font, which a design system does not carry (the owner allows the kit's PNGs, not fonts). The kit's own images of them sit in Afterburn/Icons/PNG, which this system's kit root (Afterburn/Buttons/PNG) does not reach, so its `icon` list does not name them yet (docs/ROADMAP.md); until it does, a button for one says what it does in words.

entries.claim: The README size rules say 'at least 53 px each way', 'at least 12 px between touchable controls', 'no more than nine buttons in one group' and 'GUI Designer's 10 px nudge'.

entries.reason: The 2 mm gap and the 9 mm touch minimum (53 px on the 1035) the toolkit checks between and on touch targets, and Extron's documented nine-button and 10 px standards (docs/design-rules.md section 2), which a designer's own controls keep. The Layout grows the 50 px slider to 54; the README now says the template does not always keep them.

template.does: The template's only paged list (VTC Search Results) uses up and down triangle glyphs beside the list (444,73 and 444,398, #767789). The 320 pages a device with 'More' and a chevron in the footer and a Back chevron. The words Previous and Next never appear.

entries.reason: A Group fits its members on every panel by paging them under the touch minimum and nine-button standards. Extron's triangles and chevrons are glyphs of its Afterburn icon font, which a design system does not carry; the kit draws them as images in Afterburn/Icons/PNG (Carets, Chevron), which this system's kit root (Afterburn/Buttons/PNG) does not reach yet (docs/ROADMAP.md), so the toolkit's paging says Previous and Next. The README says what the template does.
